items.title: Proposition 1.6 · convexity equivalences

source.attribution: Sinho Chewi, Lectures on Optimization. ASTIS restatement, not quoted prose; no endorsement implied.

items.statement: For a continuously differentiable real-valued function on Euclidean space and a nonnegative modulus, the chord inequality, quadratic lower model and gradient monotonicity inequality below are equivalent. Under twice continuous differentiability they are also equivalent to the Hessian bound.
assumptions: The domain is all of real d-dimensional Euclidean space; α ≥ 0.
The first three conditions use f ∈ C¹; the Hessian equivalence uses f ∈ C².
All points and directions below are universally quantified. The chord parameter lies in [0,1].

obligations.label: (1.3) → (1.4): affine segment, positive division, genuine derivative limit
(1.5) → (1.3): fundamental theorem of calculus with its regularity hypotheses
Exact whole-space C¹ three-condition equivalence and independent fidelity review
Exact C² Hessian equivalence and independent fidelity review

items.title: Proposition 1.13 · one-sided smoothness equivalences

source.anchor: §1.2, Definition1.12 equation(1.7) and Proposition1.13, both equivalence clauses
source.attribution: Sinho Chewi, Lectures on Optimization. ASTIS restatement, not quoted prose; no endorsement implied.

items.statement: For a continuously differentiable real-valued function on all Euclidean d-space and β≥0, the quadratic upper model is equivalent to the one-sided gradient bound below. With twice continuous differentiability, both are equivalent to the Hessian upper bound. The proof is omitted in the source by analogy with Proposition1.6.
assumptions: All x,y,v range over ℝᵈ; β≥0.
C¹ suffices for the first equivalence; C² is required for the Hessian clause. Convexity is not assumed.

obligations.label: Quadratic upper model ↔ one-sided gradient upper bound
Under C², quadratic upper model ↔ genuine Hessian diagonal upper bound

bindings.boundary: These are one-sided upper bounds. They do not imply a β-Lipschitz gradient without an additional condition such as convexity; no such implication is asserted here. The source instance is E=ℝᵈ and β≥0.

assumption_deltas.source: Whole Euclidean d-space and β≥0.
assumption_deltas.lean: Complete real inner-product space and arbitrary real β.
assumption_deltas.reason: The sign-reversal route uses the already available signed modulus -β. Completeness gives the genuine Riesz gradient; Euclidean spaces satisfy it, including dimension zero.

assumption_deltas.source: C¹ for the first equivalence and C² for the Hessian equivalence; proof omitted by analogy with Proposition1.6.
assumption_deltas.lean: ContDiff ℝ 1 f; actual gradient and iterated fderiv. No separately assumed symmetry, segment integrability or derivative field.
assumption_deltas.reason: Negation preserves the stated regularity. Existing signed convexity/FTC parents derive all needed interval regularity; the Hessian is represented by its bilinear evaluation.

assumption_deltas.source: One-sided upper bounds; convexity only appears in a subsequent separate Lipschitz-gradient consequence.
assumption_deltas.lean: No convexity premise or Lipschitz conclusion.
assumption_deltas.reason: The concave quadratic at β=0 is a focused boundary counterexample to conflating these conditions.
